mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during NBER-defined recessions.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the mechanism does not activate during periods of rising commodity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening in monetary and price pressures, amplifying the risk of stagflation and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when unemployment falls below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market sentiment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when mortgage rates exceed 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a statistical artifact or data inconsistency rather than genuine labor market strength, which historically coincides with market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when the apparent contradiction is resolved by subsequent data revisions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary behavior by households, which typically precedes a delayed but persistent upturn in consumer spending and ultimately positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when debt-to-income ratios are rising sharply.
